likely_cause.reasoning: Wayback snapshots show the practice's own WordPress site on this domain from Oct 2020 to Jun 2023, and a capture on 11 Jul 2025 already returns HTTP 302 to HugeDomains' domain-profile page, so control of the name changed between mid-2023 and mid-2025. RDAP today shows the registrar as TurnCommerce, Inc. DBA NameBright.com (the registrar behind HugeDomains), nameservers on NameBright DNS, expiry renewed to 27 Sep 2027 and a last-changed date of 28 Sep 2026. The creation date is still 27 Sep 2018, which means the record was not freshly created after a drop; the name appears to have passed to a domain reseller rather than being re-registered from scratch. I cannot see from public records whether the practice sold it, let the renewal lapse, or lost it in another way - that is for the owner to confirm.

fix_steps.step: Find out who holds the registrar account for crystalsmilesnj.com (the old web designer, a staff member, or the owner) and check its renewal/recovery status before doing anything else.
fix_steps.who: Owner / office manager, possibly with whoever built the old site

fix_steps.step: Decide between recovering the old name from the current holder and moving to a new domain; if a reseller price is quoted, compare it with the cost of a fresh domain name.
Remove or replace every public link that still points at the dead domain, starting with the Google Business Profile ('Add website' is showing) and directory profiles such as BizArchive.

Rebuild a small site on the new (or recovered) domain: home page, services, insurance accepted, hours, new-patient information, directions and a tap-to-call button, reusing the service list from the archived site (cleanings, implants, crowns, root canals, cosmetic, Invisalign, whitening, oral surgery).
Add an appointment request or online booking link to the new site and to the Google profile so patients can ask for a slot without calling.
Claim/verify the Google Business Profile if it is not already verified, then keep name, address, phone, hours and website consistent across directories.
Turn on domain auto-renew and expiry alerts plus simple uptime monitoring so a lapsed renewal cannot take the site down again silently.

after_fix.opportunity: Add an online appointment request (or full booking) and link it from the new site and the Google profile.
after_fix.evidence: Today the only route to the practice is the phone number: the Google profile carries the phone and hours but no website or booking link, and the archived old site's 'Book an Appointment' buttons pointed to a contact-us page rather than a scheduling tool. Rebuilding is the moment to add real self-scheduling.

severity_reason: The practice's own domain now sends visitors to a domain reseller's page instead of the office, the Google profile has no website at all, and at least one directory still publishes the dead link - so patients searching the practice name get no official page.

# Website Health Check: Crystal Smiles LLC (Dr. Tejal Darji, DMD)

## What we saw on 13 November 2026
- crystalsmilesnj.com now redirects to a HugeDomains domain page; desktop and 390 px phone visits both stopped on Cloudflare's verification screen (screenshots saved); a plain fetch returned 403.
- Wayback shows the practice's own site there from 2020 to June 2023; a July 2025 capture already redirects to HugeDomains.
- RDAP: registered 27 Sep 2018, expires 27 Sep 2027, last changed 28 Sep 2026, registrar TurnCommerce/NameBright.
- The Google profile (65 Rues Ln, (732) 257-4444, 4.8 stars) shows "Add website"; BizArchive still publishes www.crystalsmilesnj.com as the site.

## What it means for customers
A patient who searches the practice name or follows an old directory link reaches a domain reseller's page, not the office. Services, insurance, hours and directions have to come from third-party listings or a phone call.

## How to fix it
1. Establish who controls the registrar account and whether the name can be recovered (1-2 hours).
2. Remove the dead link from the Google profile and any directory still showing it (1-2 hours).
3. Put a small site on a new or recovered domain: services, insurance, hours, new patients, tap-to-call (8-16 hours).
4. Add an appointment request or booking link and connect it to the profile (2-4 hours).
5. Turn on auto-renew, expiry alerts and uptime monitoring (about 1 hour).

## After the fix
Online appointment requests let patients book outside office hours; the archived site's "Book an Appointment" buttons only opened a contact page.

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.

"When I searched Crystal Smiles today, the website address your directory listings still show took me to a domain-for-sale page - can I show you the two screenshots?"
